items.text:
Early-career resumes often aren't weak. They're unevidenced.

"Built a dashboard" says what existed—not who used it, what changed, or what you owned.

Before rewriting, ask: Who was it for? What was broken? What did I own? What changed? What can someone verify?

A polished claim is still just a claim.

The useful question isn't "How do I make this sound impressive?"

It's "What evidence would make this believable?"

That's the question I built Showcase around.

evidenceRequired: public ProofScore capacity remains configured at 25/day

Career switchers: your old work may be filed under the wrong labels.

Support can show triage + stakeholder communication.
Teaching: facilitation + measurement.
Retail: operations + conversion.

Translate honestly. Don't rename work you didn't do.

"Managed social media" is a claim. Evidence answers:

• How many channels?
• What cadence?
• What starting audience?
• Which metric changed?
• Over what period?

If you don't know, don't invent it. State the scope you can verify and start tracking the gap.

Students: metrics hide in places you stopped counting:

• project teammates
• demo users
• event attendees
• issues closed
• tests added
• load time before/after
• club budget

Use only numbers you can defend. Scope is evidence too.

Showcase is opening in small closed-beta batches, oldest signup first.

The pace follows support load, activation quality, and AI cost.

A traffic spike should lengthen the queue—not make the product worse for people already inside.

A polished portfolio can still fail the recruiter test. Ask:

• What problem?
• What did I do?
• What evidence supports the result?
• Can someone grasp it in 20 seconds?
• Is each sentence traceable to truth?

A gradient can't rescue a vague case study.

evidenceRequired: dated screenshots from an experiment on the founder's own resume

items.text:
The most dangerous resume bullet isn't the one that sounds weak.

It's the impressive one you can't defend when an interviewer asks, "How did you measure that?"

Optimize for the follow-up question, not the first glance.

Showcase tells you what stays free: create your portfolio, see your full ProofScore, preview, and edit.

Publishing a live shareable page is Pro.

No blurred work or countdown. A paywall should charge for ongoing value—not hold your own work hostage.
evidenceRequired: billing and publish paywall copy still match these entitlements

items.text:
New grads: stop describing class projects like assignments.

Weak: "Built a React app for class."

Ask: What user problem? What hard constraint? What did I own? How many teammates, tests, records, or users? Which tradeoff?

You need specific evidence—not fake impact.

10-minute resume audit:

1. Underline each claim.
2. Circle proof: numbers, scope, artifacts, outcomes, decisions.
3. Any underline without a circle? Find proof, narrow it, or delete it.

That's ProofScore. Run it free: {{url}}

No revenue metric? Don't invent one.

Scope is evidence:
• 4-person team
• 12 API endpoints
• 30 test cases
• 3-week deadline
• 2,000 records migrated

Specific, defensible context beats a fake percentage every time.

evidenceRequired: live availability is greater than zero
